bullets.md: **The first part of high availability in a region. It stays off until you turn it on.** A new console setting, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, lists the regions whose new instances are born highly available. Such an instance can wake on any box in its region, and only one box serves it at a time. This release turns it on nowhere. Instances that exist today keep working exactly as before, and are never converted.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.23 or earlier, read the [v0.28.24 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.24) first, and the notes they point to.

**The box agent changes.** Each lease lock now names the box, its instance id when known, and the process id. For instances that exist today, the lock is still deleted when the instance sleeps. For an instance born highly available, the box writes a release marker instead of deleting the lock. Another box takes the instance only after a clean marker. A box reuses its own local copy only when the marker names that box, the lifetime matches, and the local state is unchanged. Otherwise it restores the instance from storage. Such an instance runs only in the nested layout. A box that cannot run it nested refuses the wake.

**Moves and places refuse highly available instances. Imports into a highly available region refuse.** An offline move of one and `carlos apps place` for its app are refused before anything stops. An import into a highly available region is refused before anything is written.

**`carlos system join` is gone.** Joining mode, its units `carlos-system-join.path` and `carlos-system-join.service`, and the console's enrolment pass are removed. Bootstrapping a box removes those units if an earlier build left them.

bullets.md: **Edges can keep copies of an app's asset folders.** On an armed box, the edge can keep copies of cacheable files under the folders an app declares with `carlos deploy --assets` or `carlos ship --assets`, and answer later matching requests from those copies. An armed box in another region can fill its copy from the app's home box, so a visitor far from home can get the file from a nearer box. For cache-eligible requests, `Carlos-Cache` is `miss` when the box fetched the file for a cache fill, even if the copy was not ultimately stored, `hit` when it answered from its copy, and `bypass` when it forwarded the request without using the cache. Nothing is copied until an operator arms a box.

**The console can show CPU and memory for non-isolated instances on other boxes.** This works when the box can confirm that the instance was started for that tenant and remained that tenant while the sample was read. Instances that run inside nested groups, and isolated instances on other boxes, still show no readings.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.16 or earlier, read the [v0.28.17 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.17) first.

**The console, CLI, and router binary change, and so does the box agent.** The agent marks samples from a non-isolated instance only when it can confirm that the instance was started for that tenant and remained that tenant while the sample was read. The console uses a reading from another box only when that mark matches the instance, and an older console ignores the mark.

**The asset cache stays off until you arm a box.** To arm one, set `CARLOS_ASSET_CACHE=1` in its host.env and restart it. The copies live in `asset-cache` under the box's data directory. They take at most 4 GiB or a tenth of the data filesystem, whichever is smaller. A positive `CARLOS_ASSET_CACHE_MAX` value sets the size in bytes instead. Only an armed home box publishes an app's assets to other boxes. In dev, arm the home box for a test app first. Then arm one box in another region and verify that it can fetch the app's asset from the home box before arming the rest. On the flagship, arm the console box first, then one small box and watch its disk, then the rest one at a time.

bullets.md: **`carlos deploy` and `carlos canary` can check a host behind a password gate.** Deploy asks the console for a pass that lasts 15 minutes and checks the new version through the gate with it. The console only hands one to someone who could already remove the gate, or to a deploy credential for a host on a channel it can deploy its own build to, and each one is recorded in the app's activity log.

**The edge records requests for well-known attack paths.** It checks each request against a list built into the platform, such as `.env` and `.git` files, path traversal and common probe paths. By default it blocks nothing: a match is recorded and the request goes on to the app. `carlos explain <code> --app <a>` says which rule fired and when, and shows the request if it is still kept, for up to 7 days.
**An offline move's pause is a few seconds shorter.** At the first wake after a move opens, the new box removes the staged copy's files 8 at a time instead of one by one.

The box's isolation probe now also checks that deny (`box-addr`) and that a nested instance using the default memory setting cannot map memory that is both writable and executable (`mdwe`). bullets.md: **An instance can have rate limits.** `carlos ratelimit show` displays four numbers per instance, while `set` and `clear` change them for one instance or every instance of an app: when it counts as busy, how many requests one address may have in flight while it is busy, and a backstop rate and burst per address. A path prefix such as `/api/` can have its own share, rate and burst. A refused visitor gets `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`, and a refused request never wakes a sleeping instance. In the default observe mode, a box only counts what it would refuse until the deployment's operator turns enforcement on. The docs' "Rate limits" page says more.

**A new custom domain gets checked for a certificate sooner.** Once a host is attached, the certificate issuer checks its DNS every minute for ten minutes, then every five minutes for the rest of the hour. If DNS points at the deployment, it can order the certificate before the next hourly pass, subject to the shared certificate order limit.

**The edge keeps request records in an app's logs.** It records a sample of requests that found nothing. It keeps path pieces and query parameter names only when they are short or look like harmless lower-case words, and masks the rest. It also records a count of the app's requests each minute. `carlos logs --stream edge` shows them.

**Static sites: old cache versions are cleaned up at startup when the edge is alone.** On the first start that creates the cache lock, the edge only creates the lock. A later start can set aside old release trees and remove them in the background when no other edge is serving the cache.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.14 or earlier, read the [v0.28.15 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.15) first.

**Rate limits only count until you set `CARLOS_RATE_LIMIT=enforce`.** Each box reads it from its `host.env`. Unset or `observe`, a box counts and logs what it would refuse and refuses nothing. `off` turns the limiter off. Read the counts with `carlos ratelimit show` for a few days, then set `enforce`, dev boxes first.

**Disk use under `/data/static` can drop after the second edge start on this release.** At startup, an edge that is the only one using its static cache sets aside old release trees and removes them in the background, while keeping each site's current version. The first start on this release only creates the cache's lock file, so cleanup starts from the next start.

**Plan caps still do nothing without a plan catalog.** With `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` set, a console now refuses new always-on workers and schedules that run more often than the plan allows on shared boxes, while allowing them on an account's own boxes. **The `deployment-buckets` and `region-remote-host` modules expire old data versions.** In their data buckets, a replaced or deleted version is kept for 7 days (`data_noncurrent_days`) before it expires. On a box with over a hundred instances that took longer than the 20 seconds the update allows, so the box rolled back after about half a minute of failed requests. The keys are now written in the background once the edge is serving, and the update no longer waits for them.
**Nothing changes for people using the CLI.**
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.**

**Coming from v0.25.x, read the [v0.26.0 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.26.0) first.** They all still apply, and that includes any box that rolled back from v0.26.0. Restart `carlos-instance-control.service` on each box after it updates, run the instance key checks before any box rolls, and check what root's AWS settings rely on (#267).

**Wait for the instance key line.** `agent: instance keys:` now comes after `hibernation activator armed`, up to about a minute after the agent starts. Wait for it before you check for `0 failed`. It also counts rows skipped because a move or a layout change held the host. Those get their key at their next start.

**Every dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_SWAP`, `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS` and `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST` unset, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. The v0.26.0 notes say where each one is set.

bullets.md: **Two builds at once, off until your deployment turns it on.** Where it is on, a new build starts beside the old one and takes over once it passes its health check, so no request waits. For a few seconds both builds share the instance's database and its scheduled work, and the new build's migrations run while the old one still serves. So add a column, table or index in one release and drop the old one in a later release. Keep the names of scheduled work (`carlos schedule`) the same across the two builds. A release that can't follow these rules ships with `--swap hold` on `carlos deploy` or `carlos ship`, which stops each instance before its new build starts. `carlos apps set <app> --swap hold` makes that the app's rule, and `--swap-concurrency` sets how many instances swap at once on one box. Every deployment ships with this off.

**`carlos deploy` follows the rollout box by box.** Where a box reports its rollout, deploy counts an awake instance once the new build has passed its health check and taken over, and an asleep one once its box has installed the build. If the build fails on a box, that box stops rolling it out, and deploy names the failure and exits with an error. Boxes report only where two builds at once is on. Everywhere else deploy watches the app's URL, as before. If the console can't list the app's instances, deploy keeps asking until its deadline and then says the list could not be read.

**`carlos instances list` shows two builds.** INSTALLED is the build on the instance's box, and SERVING is the one answering its requests. They differ while a build rolls out, while an asleep instance waits for its next request, and after a build has failed on that box. REASON says which. A dash under SERVING means the box doesn't report it, which is every box until two builds at once is on. `carlos instances retry <host>` clears the failure hold on one instance, so the build that failed there is tried again as a canary.

**Choose how each instance takes new builds.** `carlos instances set <host> --updates manual` stops an instance taking new builds on its own. `--channel`, `--major` (stable only) and `--pin <build>` set the rest, and an empty value goes back to the app's default. `carlos instances update <host>` asks the box to install the newest build it considers ready, even with manual updates. `--fast-track` skips the safety delay, and only account owners can use it. On the app, `carlos apps set --instance-control updates,pin` names the settings an instance may change for itself once instances can act for themselves. `--default-updates`, `--default-major` and `--default-channel` set the app's defaults. The console accepts manual updates, a major hold or a pin only once every box can keep the builds they name, and says how many boxes it is waiting for.

**Read a database as it was.** `carlos db pull --at <time>` and `carlos db query --at <time>` read an instance's database as it was at an earlier time, given in RFC 3339 form such as `2026-10-07T14:00:00Z`. The copy is never newer than that time, and the command says which transaction it stopped at. Ask for a time before the oldest history and it names the oldest time you can use. Instances that sleep now keep seven days of history, as awake ones do. That week fills in over the seven days after your deployment rolls this release.

**Channel digests.** `carlos channels digests` shows whether channel pointers carry the sha256 of each build's manifest, and lists the channels that don't yet. Once a deployment turns digests on, boxes refuse pointers without them. So update the CLI on every machine and CI job that promotes, rolls back or fast-tracks before then. `carlos channels resign <channel>` re-signs a channel nobody has promoted to since digests went on. It shows every digest and signs only when you type yes.

**`carlos releases authorize <app> <version>`, for operators.** It shows a build's manifest and file digests and, when you type yes, signs a promotion record for exactly those bytes. Every promotion now writes one. This is for a build promoted before records existed, so an instance can be pinned to it or recovered onto it.

**What an instance is started with.** Every instance and seed now gets `CARLOS_HOST`, its hostname exactly as `carlos instances list` shows it. Read it, never the socket's file name. On an isolated box, an instance starts in its own data directory, the one its database is in, so a relative path such as `./data/blobs` lands beside its database. Files and directories named after the host, such as `<host>/` or `<host>-blobs`, now move with an instance when its box isolates it, and come back on a revert.

**`carlos move`, off until your deployment turns moves on.** It moves one instance to another region. The instance keeps serving while its data is copied, then goes offline for the cut. If the new region can't start it, the move takes it back on its own. Against a console without moves, `carlos move` sends nothing.

**Smaller fixes.** A build of about 100 MB no longer runs the box's staging out of memory, so its promote no longer waits for the hourly pass. `carlos sidecars ls` shows the build each sidecar's box last started, and "unknown" for one that hasn't started anywhere. `carlos instances set-channel` finds a host typed with capitals, and for a box route with no instance record it says how to move the route on its box.
**If your boxes haven't run v0.25.1, read its operator notes and v0.25.0's first.** They all apply to this release.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Roll the boxes with `carlos system update`.

**After each box updates, restart `carlos-instance-control.service` on it.** The update runs the code the box already has, which installs this release without restarting that service. This release's agent refuses to wake isolated instances while the service runs an older build, and the reason in `carlos logs` ends with `restart carlos-instance-control.service`. `carlos system status` still reads `current`, so it won't tell you. From this release on, `carlos system update` restarts the service itself.

**Before any box rolls, run the instance key checks.** This release writes a `CARLOS_INSTANCE_KEY` into each instance's `<host>.env` the first time it starts, and starts a replica only with its home's key.
items: On every box, `find <data> -maxdepth 1 -name '*.env' -type l` must print nothing. A `<host>.env` that is a symlink now fails that instance's start. Stop the instance, replace the link with the real file, and treat the token in it as leaked.

On every box with a replica (`sqlite3 <data>/registry.db "select host from routes where replica=1"`), compare each replica's key with its home's. A key is the last `CARLOS_INSTANCE_KEY` line of `<host>.env`, or of `<host>.config.env` when `<host>.env` has none, in the data directory for a flat instance or the instance's own directory for an isolated one. Where the two match, add `<replica-host>=<sha256 of the key>` to `/etc/carlos/replica-home-keys` on the replica's box before it rolls. Write the whole list to a temporary file in `/etc/carlos`, make it root:carlos 0640, and rename it into place. Where they differ, the replica is refused after the roll. Tell its owner first.
A replica with no key keeps starting where it has a control socket, but its legacy sidecar and any worker row of its own stop at the roll. List them on each box with a replica, and tell their owners.
Check the agent can read the list: `sudo -u <agent user> test -r /etc/carlos/replica-home-keys && echo ok` must print `ok`.
After the roll, `journalctl -u carlos-edge --since '<roll time>' | grep 'agent: instance keys:'` must show `0 failed`.

bullets.md: **Root ignores AWS profile, endpoint and trust-store settings.** A box's root processes now ignore `AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, `AWS_CA_BUNDLE`, the `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` variables, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` and shared AWS config files, and log an alert when one is set. Before rolling, check that no box's host.env depends on them. On a box outside AWS, `/etc/carlos/credentials` must hold only static keys under `[default]`. The agent rewrites it as root:carlos 0640 on every start.
**Every dormant switch stays off.** Leave each of these unset, and run none of the commands named, until its own rollout is approved.
items: `CARLOS_SWAP` on every box. Two builds at once still has open items, and only the exact word `overlap` arms it.
`CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1` on the console and every box. Don't publish a moves protocol floor (`control/moves-protocol.json`) either.

`CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS` and `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS` on the console and every box, and `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID` on the console. Don't run `carlos system guard-arm` or `carlos system journal-migrate`.
`CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST` on every box. Don't run `carlos channels digests on` yet.

bullets.md: **Host claims: every roster reader first.** Binaries older than this release reject a signed roster that names a home region. So before anyone publishes the home designation, every reader of `control/host-actors.json` must run this release: every console, every box's agent and root services, the update and rollback tools, and any offline or recovery binary. The designation is write-once, and this roll doesn't publish it.

**Digests: writers before readers.** Once a box has verified a channel pointer with digests, it refuses pointers for that channel without them. So first upgrade every writer: every console, and every CLI or deploy script that promotes, rolls back or fast-tracks. Then run `carlos channels digests on`, and watch `carlos channels digests` until it lists nothing. Only then set `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST=on` in every box's host.env. `carlos channels digests off` stops writers adding digests while one is fixed, but doesn't clear boxes that have already seen them.

**Instance update settings wait for every box.** The console refuses manual updates, a major hold or a pin until every box reports it can keep the builds they name. Before rolling any box back below this release, run `carlos releases retention --off` for each app that has a retention policy, because an older box prunes builds a pin or a held instance still needs. After such a rollback the console shows *settings not enforced* for instances on the older boxes.

**Remove the staging memory drop-ins after the roll.** Staging now streams a build to disk instead of reading it into memory. A deployment that raised the memory of `carlos-stage.service` or `carlos-adopt.service` with a drop-in can remove it from every box, and from its box bootstrap, once every box runs this release.

**The `deployment-buckets` module now guards fence writes.** Its new statement refuses every write under `control/box-fences/` from a role not listed in `box_fence_writer_role_arns`. Nothing writes there while host claims are off, so applying it now is safe.

**Files left behind by earlier moves.** An instance its box isolated before this release may have left files named after its host in the shared data directory. `carlos status --layout` and the agent log now name them on every pass. Move them into the instance's directory by hand.

changelog: v0.25.0 (release step 10)

bullets.md: **Isolated instances now happen.** v0.25.0 moved instances into their own box only on a box whose isolation probe passed, and no box could pass. Part of the probe checked the box's addresses using a kind of socket the probe's own unit is not allowed to open. The control service now makes that check itself, reading the addresses from `/proc`. Boxes whose other checks pass are now ready, and their instances move as v0.25.0 described.

**Isolated instances stop cleanly.** Inside its own box, an app ran as the first process, where the kernel ignores any signal the app has no handler for. A Go app with no SIGTERM handler could not be stopped: each stop waited 20 seconds, killed it, and left the unit failed. A small init now runs first. It passes stop signals on to the app, cleans up exited processes, and exits with the app's status. An app that dies by a signal now shows as `exit 128+n` in its instance event line, so a crash on SIGSEGV reads `instance exited: exit 139`. It used to read `signal`.

**Temporary static sites, off until a deployment turns them on.** `carlos deploy --temporary ./dist` creates an app named `tmp-` plus six letters and digits, or `tmp-<name>` with `--app <name>`. It lives 7 days, or what `--ttl` says (1h to 30d). When its time is up it moves to the Trash, and it is purged 3 days later instead of 30. `carlos apps ttl` moves the expiry and `carlos apps keep` makes it permanent. A temporary app is served only at its own platform address, so `--host` and `--kind binary` are refused, and an account holds at most 20.
**Names starting with `tmp-` are reserved** for temporary sites. `carlos apps create`, `carlos add --app`, renames and `console grant` refuse them, whether or not temporary sites are on.
**`carlos apps list`** shows every app in the account, the Trash included, and when each expires or is purged.

**`carlos ship` checks the program.** For a Go binary, ship records its main package in the manifest. It refuses a release whose main package differs from the app's latest release. When the change is meant, ship with `--program-change`. `carlos deploy` has no such flag, so use `carlos ship --program-change` and then promote. Boxes check the bytes too, so a release shipped by an older client is refused at adoption and is not pointed live. A build the route has run before is always accepted, so going back across an intended change works.

**A console that will not start is rolled back.** After a box adopts a new build for a route with a named unit, such as the console, it waits for the unit to stay up and accept connections. If it doesn't, the box rolls back, refuses that promotion and alerts. A plain re-promote stays refused. `carlos promote --retry <version> <channel>` tries again. `carlos status --live` shows refused hosts.

**GeoIP for apps.** On a deployment that has published a GeoIP database, every request to an app carries the visitor's rough location in `X-Carlos-Geo-Country`, `X-Carlos-Geo-Subdivision`, `X-Carlos-Geo-Lat`, `X-Carlos-Geo-Lon` and `X-Carlos-Geo-Source`. Any of them can be missing; treat that as unknown. The edge removes any of these a visitor sends. Analytics count page views by country and credit the database. `carlos geo <address> --app <a>` gives the same answer for any address, and apps can call `GET /api/cli/apps/<account>/<app>/geo?ip=<address>`, at most 60 a minute. An app that shows visitors anything worked out from these headers must credit the database `X-Carlos-Geo-Source` names.
**If your boxes have not run v0.25.0, read its operator notes first.** All of them apply to this release.

**Instances move to the nested layout on their own, and this time they will.** v0.25.0's note applies again. With no layout intent recorded, every box whose isolation probe passes starts moving its instances on the first change it sees after this release lands. Awake instances get an hour, then are stopped and moved. This includes boxes that already run v0.25.0 and recorded nothing. **To keep control,** record `carlos system layout revert` before you roll, then `carlos system layout migrate --box <label>` one box at a time, or put `CARLOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT=flat` in a box's host.env to leave that box alone.

**Before rolling, check one box:** `systemctl start carlos-instance-probe.service` then read `/run/carlos-control/probe.out`. It must say `ready: true`. The control service no longer opens a resolver that is one of the box's own addresses. It reports that as a failing `resolver-local` line, and if it cannot read the box's addresses it opens no resolver at all. Landlock must be in the booted kernel's `lsm=` list, and `/etc/resolv.conf` (or resolved's upstream list) must name a resolver that isn't on loopback.
**Roll the boxes before the console.** The rollback, wrong-program and `tmp-` checks run on the box, and so does removing forged GeoIP headers.

**Fix each console box's binding before you rely on the rollback.** The rollback check runs only when the console unit's `ExecStart` names the live link of the route stamped with that unit. Where it doesn't, `adopt` logs `binding: … restart not checked` and restarts the unit as before, unchecked. On each console box, read `systemctl show -p ExecStart console.service`, stamp that host with `carlos route --host <host> --unit console.service`, and clear the stamp from any other host with `--unit ""`. Until the binding is right, keep the final `systemctl restart` in your console roll.

**The rollback check is on everywhere.** After adopting a build for a route with a named unit, the box waits up to 30 seconds (`CARLOS_UNIT_SETTLE`, at least 5s) for the unit to stay up on the new build and accept connections. If it does not, the box rolls back, writes a refusal and alerts through SNS or `CARLOS_ALERT_WEBHOOK`. If your console takes longer than that to start listening, raise `CARLOS_UNIT_SETTLE` on its box before you fix the binding. With `CONSOLE_GEOIP_DB` set, the console now checks that file in a separate process before it listens.

**The wrong-program check is on everywhere.** A box refuses a staged binary whose Go main package differs from the live build's and from every program that route has run before, unless its manifest records `--program-change`. The refused build is not pointed live and nothing restarts. Each route starts its history from its live binary on its first pass. The console's ship door makes the same check once the console runs this release. The `carlos` binary is never a console artifact; build the console from `./cmd/console`.

**Dev proofs are off.** They are off unless a box has `/etc/carlos/proof-policy.json` (root, mode 0644). On a proving console box, run `carlos proof keygen` as root, then write a policy file with a `prove` block: the apps, the prover's name, how long a build must run (`after`, such as 15m) and `key_file`. That box then mints a proof for each build that runs healthily for that long. On a requiring box, a `require` entry names the app, the prover and its public key. A new build of that app is then adopted only with a proof for those exact bytes, or if the box has already run that build healthily. Carry a proof with `carlos proof get` against the proving deployment and `carlos proof put` against the requiring one. `carlos status --live` shows a host that is waiting. A policy file that does not parse holds every named-unit route on its current build and says so in the journal. To switch the requirement off, delete the `require` entry (or the file) as root and run `carlos adopt --stage-only`. The box then logs once an hour that it is off. Write policy files on the box over SSM, not through tofu `user_data`.

**Temporary sites are off until you set `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS=1` on the console.** The console adds four columns to its `apps` table when it starts. The change is additive. Its expiry pass runs every 5 minutes either way, and with no temporary apps it does nothing. Before you turn them on, roll every box, then check that no box's registry and neither the console's `apps` nor its `owners` table has a `tmp-` name. An expiry drops a temporary app's routes, so rename or remove any `tmp-` name you find first.

**Platform GeoIP sends nothing until you publish a database.** From this release every edge removes forged `X-Carlos-Geo-` headers and watches the bucket for a database. `carlos system geoip publish <file.mmdb>` sends one, and every edge picks it up within 12 minutes. Publish only after `carlos system geoip status` says `ready`, because a box on an older release passes a visitor's forged headers straight through. A retired box that still has `control/edges/<label>.json` keeps it from saying `ready`; delete that record. `carlos system geoip off` removes the database. On the console box, check that the console can read `/data/carlos/geoip/current`: with `CONSOLE_GEOIP_DB` unset, the console's region guess now uses that copy.

**The GeoIP feed is off until you set `CONSOLE_GEOIP_FEED`.** `dbip-city-lite` is free, needs nothing else, and requires the credit the platform already shows. bullets.md: **Each instance runs in its own box.** Instances the platform starts on demand used to share one user and one data directory on a box, so one app could read another app's files. From this release, a box whose isolation checks pass moves every such instance into its own directory and its own mount and process namespace, where it sees its own files and nothing else. A sleeping instance moves at once; an awake one gets an hour to go to sleep, then is stopped briefly and moved. New instances on that box start out isolated. `carlos status --layout` shows where each box is.
**`carlos system layout`** lets an operator choose instead: `migrate --box <label>` moves one box at a time, and `revert` moves everything back. `status` prints what is recorded.

**Instances get CPU and IO limits** beside their memory cap, see only their own app's build, and can't reach loopback or private addresses on the box except its DNS resolver. New starts are refused while the disk is nearly full.

**Custom domains can require proof.** On a deployment that sets `CONSOLE_DOMAIN_PROOF=true`, `carlos domains attach` reserves the name and prints a TXT record, and the name isn't served until `carlos domains verify` finds it. Names under another account's platform domain are refused everywhere.
**Only a platform operator can add an upstream address** to an instance. Upstreams an instance already has keep working, and can be kept, reordered or removed.
**Cookies stay within their account.** On a platform hostname, a cookie whose `Domain` reaches beyond the app's own account is made host-only by the edge.
**Instance catch-all domains.** `carlos domains attach --app <a> '*.<parent>'` gives every instance of the app a public name, `<slug>.<parent>`, with no per-instance claim or DNS.

**`carlos email test` sends HTML too.** The test message is now multipart, with a plain-text and an HTML part, so it shows that HTML mail gets through. Apps can send any MIME message over their credential.

**Smaller fixes.** Re-attaching a static site's own hostname to flip `--wildcard` or `--catchall` no longer turns its route into an alias of itself. A box no longer places a certificate order every hour for a platform domain whose DNS zone its provider doesn't hold.

**Instances move to the nested layout on their own.** This is the first release on which isolated instances run. With no layout intent recorded, every box whose isolation probe passes starts moving its instances on the first change it sees after this release lands. Awake instances get an hour, then are stopped and moved. A move refused for a reason a tenant could have caused (a planted hard link, a symlinked directory) keeps that instance stopped until an operator clears it; `carlos status --layout` names it. **To keep control,** record `carlos system layout revert` before you roll, then `carlos system layout migrate --box <label>` one box at a time, or put `CARLOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT=flat` in a box's host.env to leave that box alone.

**Before rolling, check one box:** `systemctl start carlos-instance-probe.service` then read `/run/carlos-control/probe.out`. It must say `ready: true`. Landlock must be in the booted kernel's `lsm=` list, and `/etc/resolv.conf` (or resolved's upstream list) must name a resolver that isn't on loopback. A box that fails any of these stays flat and says why.

**Roll the boxes before the console.** The console now trusts a loopback `X-Forwarded-For` only when the edge has signed it, and switches to requiring the signature after it first sees one. Domain proof needs boxes that understand pending claims.

**Rolling back** to a release before v0.25.0 is refused while any box has nested instances. Run `carlos system layout revert`, wait until `carlos status --layout` shows every instance `flat`, then roll back.

**Settings worth turning on** for a deployment that hosts other people's apps: `CONSOLE_DOMAIN_PROOF=true` and `CONSOLE_RESERVE_PLATFORM_DOMAINS=true` on the console, after the boxes have rolled. `CONSOLE_SECRETS_ENVELOPE_V2=true` makes new secrets bound to their account and app; set it only once every box runs this release.

bullets.md: **CI can deploy through the console.** `carlos services create --role deploy --app <a> --rungs canary,edge <name>` mints a credential that can ship, and promote or roll back only the rungs you name: `canary`, `edge` and `beta`, never `stable`. In CI, set `CARLOS_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_CONSOLE` and run `carlos deploy` as usual. The first deploy of a new app still needs a person, because a deploy credential cannot create the app or set up its first host. It cannot hotfix, delete the app, or change retention or domains. `carlos services list` gains a RUNGS column. The CLI refuses to run with both `CARLOS_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_BUCKET` or `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_DIR` set.
**A failed rollback says so.** When the console cannot sign a rollback, it now answers "Nothing was rolled back." Before, it said "Nothing was promoted."
**`carlos db` no longer panics.** If `carlos db pull` or `query` could not create its temporary file, the restore crashed. It now reports the error.

**The boxes come back onto the release train.** The flagship boxes have been running a hotfix build of v0.23.0 (f3f6cf73). It carried four fixes. Three are in v0.24.0, and their operator notes are there: a box runs its adopt work on its own loop, lists the bucket by app, and reads in parallel. The fourth is new in this release. When a box cannot stage a release itself, it asks a root pass to do it. That request used to be sent at most once a minute, and one made inside the minute was dropped, so a second release soon after the first waited for the next change to be noticed. On the flagship that was 98 extra seconds. The request is now limited to once every 15 seconds, and one made inside that window is sent at its end instead of dropped. Rolling this release moves those boxes off the hotfix with nothing lost.

**If your boxes are coming from v0.23.0 or a hotfix of it, read v0.24.0's operator notes first.** Its changes now apply to the boxes: the keyless config guard, the box with no deployment store, and alerts to SNS. The check that matters most is this one. Every box that runs placed instances must hold the right `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY` before you roll. A box without it, or with a key that does not open an instance's sealed config, will not wake that instance.

**Leave `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` unset on the console.** Any value that is not blank turns it on, including `0` and `false`. The console reads it once, when it starts. Nothing writes host claims yet, so with it on, `carlos db pull` and `carlos db query` fail for every host.

**Do not set `CARLOS_REGION_HA` on a box yet.** It is the switch for multi-box regions, which this release does not finish. Left unset, a box publishes no `region-ha-1` capability and no headroom, and nothing changes.

**Deploy credentials need the console's signing key.** The console signs each deploy promote with a grant limited to the credential's rungs, so the console must hold its release key, as it already does for promotes. It adds a `rungs` column to its `cli_tokens` table when it starts. The change is additive.

**Region HA foundations ship dormant.** Every box's edges file gains `box_id`, which is the box's label. Box bootstrap also creates `/run/carlos/hostguard` and `/data/hostguard`, mode 2770, owned by `carlos:carlos`, when tmpfiles next runs. Nothing uses them yet. The host claim, generation selection and park libraries have no callers, so the boxes behave as before.

**Read the plan before applying the infrastructure modules.** `region-host` gains a termination queue, an EventBridge rule and a box-role policy to read the queue, and its root volume is now deleted when the instance terminates. `deployment-buckets` gains a bucket policy that makes `control/boxes/*` create-only and undeletable. A bucket holds one policy, so check whether yours already has one before you apply. Nothing in this release needs them, so applying can wait. The own-bucket S3 version grants are split into separately named statements, with the same permissions.
**The scanner host fix is in this release too.** It is the freshclam change from v0.24.1.
**Either roll order works.** Nothing in this release needs the console and the boxes to roll in a particular order.

bullets.md: **Canaries have a one-label address, and can be created again.** A canary's host is now `<name>-<app>.<your account>.<apps domain>`, so canary `new-queue` of app `jam` is `new-queue-jam.bab.oncarlos.com`. The old address put a dot between the name and the app. The console refused that, so `carlos canary` could not create a canary for an app that runs a process. The name and the app together can be at most 63 characters. You need this release's CLI.

**Deploys reach running instances sooner on busy boxes.** A box notices a promote sooner, and it restarts an awake instance onto the new release on its own two-second check instead of waiting for the rest of its work. On the flagship, noticing a promote had taken 16 to 43 seconds, and the restart then waited about 48 seconds more.

**An instance never starts without its secrets.** A box that cannot open an instance's sealed secrets no longer wakes it or takes it on. A box that can takes it instead. If none can, it does not start. Before, it could start with none of its config or secrets.

**One address, one app.** `carlos instances create` and `carlos canary` are refused when another app in your account already holds the host, including an app in the Trash, or when the host is a domain attached to another app. Before, both creates succeeded and one of them served nothing.
**Nothing new to type.** The CLI has no new commands or flags in this release.

**Check every box's secrets key before rolling the boxes.** A box now takes an exec instance only if it can open that instance's sealed config. Without `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY`, or with a key that does not open the config, it does not wake the instance or mint its record. It logs `agent: config guard: refusing <host>` and lists the host under `metrics.config_refusals` in its private snapshot, `status/boxes/<box>.json`. A box that cannot read the deployment store to check refuses too, and asks again after 30 seconds. Instances with no sealed config are not affected.

**A box with no deployment store refuses exec instances.** With `CARLOS_HIBERNATE_BUCKET` set and neither `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_BUCKET` nor `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_DIR`, a box cannot tell whether an instance's config is sealed, so it refuses. On a deployment with no sealed config at all, set `CARLOS_NO_SEALED_CONFIG=1`. Never set it on a box that serves tenants. The box then logs that the check is bypassed and says so in its snapshot. With a deployment store configured, the setting is ignored.

**Roll the console to this release before pointing it at a scanner host.** An older console records an archive that clamd could only partly scan as infected. This release records it as not scanned, and a scan time-out as failed, so the next sweep tries it again. A real signature match is still infected.

**Object-storage scanning has its own box.** The new `infra/modules/scanner-host` module runs clamd on one box per deployment, reachable only from the console's security group. Set its outputs on the console: `clamd_addr` as `CARLOS_CLAMD_ADDR` and `stream_max_bytes` as `CARLOS_CLAMD_MAX_BYTES`. The console also needs `CARLOS_SCAN_TAG_KEY`, and refuses to boot with an address and no key. Set `store_scanning = true` on the console box's `region-host` so its role can read and tag store objects. It is off by default, and a deployment that leaves it off plans no change. Wiring the engine does not switch scanning on. `carlos system antivirus enable` does. A replaced scanner box gets a new private IP, so update `CARLOS_CLAMD_ADDR` after any `-replace`. Pin modules to v0.24.0: v0.23.0 does not contain `scanner-host`.
**The app regions rollback floor is v0.23.0.** v0.23.0 is the first release that understands app regions. Once any app holds a region other than the home, do not roll the console below v0.23.0.

**Boxes can send alerts to SNS.** Set `CARLOS_ALERT_SNS_TOPIC_ARN` to the box's own region's alerts topic, and anyone subscribed gets each fire and clear by email. The box's instance role needs `sns:Publish` on that topic. The modules in this repo do not grant it. A box with neither this nor `CARLOS_ALERT_WEBHOOK` logs `NO SINK CONFIGURED` when it starts. `carlos status --live` gains a last column: `alerts=sns`, `alerts=webhook`, `alerts=webhook+sns`, `alerts=not-delivered`, or `alerts=sns-unavailable` when a topic is set but the box could not build its SNS client. A dash means the box runs an older release.

**Boxes list the bucket by app.** To find instance records, a box now lists each account's apps and each app's `instances/` prefix, eight requests at a time, instead of every object under `apps/`. If one app's listing fails, the box logs a `provision: listing` line, converges everything it did see, and removes no route on that pass. The agent also logs an `agent: fast converge:` line when a step of its fast loop takes longer than five seconds.
**Either roll order works.** Nothing in this release needs the console and the boxes to roll in a particular order.

bullets.md: **A deploy reaches a running instance in seconds.** When a box adopts a new release, an instance that is awake restarts onto it within a few seconds. Before, it kept serving the old build for about two minutes, longer than `carlos deploy` waits, so a deploy could report a timeout and a restart seemed to be needed. Instances on one box restart one at a time, two seconds apart.

**Static sites show a deploy on the next page load.** Browsers now check with the edge before reusing a page or file from a static site, and get a quick "not modified" answer while nothing has changed. Before, a browser could keep showing the old page for hours or days after a deploy.

**Read a copy of an instance's database.** `carlos db pull --app <a> --out <file>` saves a copy of a sleeping instance's database on your machine, and `carlos db query --app <a> --sql "…"` runs one query against a fresh copy. Both say how recent the copy is. The copy is read-only and never touches the live database. Name an instance with `--instance` when the app has more than one.

**Region flags.** `carlos apps create`, `carlos deploy` and `carlos canary` take `--region`. A console that is not assigning app regions yet says so and starts the app in its home region. `carlos deploy --region` on an existing app stops before shipping if the region differs from the app's own. The line `carlos instances create` prints now names the place the instance runs.
**Invite links ask before you join.** Opening an invite link shows who invited you and a Join button. Nothing happens until you press it.

**Sending domains you did not set up.** If a domain already has a sending identity that your account did not create, `carlos email domains add` asks you to prove you control it: publish a TXT record at `_carlos-mail.<domain>` with the value `carlos-mail-account=<account>`, then add the domain again. A domain another account holds now reads "sending domain unavailable". A claim that is not verified within 7 days can be taken by another account.

**Stores no longer share a bucket by accident.** App and environment names are joined with "-", so app `shop` with environment `eu` and app `shop-eu` used to map to the same bucket. The second one is now refused with a 409, and nothing is created.
**Platform domains.** An operator can attach one of the deployment's own domains to an app with `carlos domains attach --platform`. Members cannot attach, change or detach those names.
**Roll the boxes, then the console.** With the new switches left off, either order is safe. The two switches below need every box on v0.23.0 first.

**Leave `CONSOLE_SECRETS_ENVELOPE_V2` off until every box runs v0.23.0.** When it is on, the console seals new secrets so they open only for their own account and app. A box on an older release cannot open them, and the app's whole config stops updating on that box. Rolling a box back below v0.23.0 after turning it on does the same. A value that is not true or false stops the console from starting.

**v0.23.0 is the first release that understands app regions.** That makes it the rollback floor the README describes: once any app holds a region other than the home, do not roll the console below v0.23.0. `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS` is off by default. Turn it on only by the README's steps. Boxes now publish `serves_shared_pool`, `accepts_inbound` and, where they hold the secrets key, `secrets_key_fp` in their edges file.

**Boxes restart awake instances when they adopt a release.** The agent checks every two seconds and restarts at most one instance per check. Workers still converge on the old 90-second timer. A restart drains the old process as before: new requests wait for the new one.

**Static responses change their headers.** They now carry `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a weak `ETag` worked out from each file's bytes and type, and no `Last-Modified`. The first request for a file after a deploy reads it once to work out the tag. The edge's own cache still does not store static responses.

**Pin infrastructure modules to v0.23.0.** The box role gains permission to list, read and delete object versions in its own data bucket. Nothing uses it yet, so applying it can wait. Check also that nothing in your policies denies `s3:DeleteObject` on the deployment bucket: purges, store teardown and mail claim release delete objects, and fail without it.

**Run `carlos accounts migrate` with a v0.23.0 CLI.** Pointers are now signed for their account, and migrating re-signs them, which needs the root `CARLOS_RELEASE_KEY`. An older CLI copies them unchanged, and the moved app stops adopting releases.

**Existing data is left in place.** Purging an app now also deletes its tokens, door keys and ledgers, but apps purged before this release keep theirs. Removing a sending domain that was added before this release leaves its SES identity in SES. Moving an app revokes its door keys, so moved apps need new ones.

bullets.md: **Database size on the app Overview.** A new tile shows how much disk your app's databases use, including copies that are asleep.

**Busy and large instances can finish a move.** An instance that is awake and writing, or that keeps large database files, can now finish moving to another region. Before, such a move could wait in `preparing` and never become ready. The cut still copies everything that is left, exactly, before the instance serves from its new region.
**Nothing new to type.** The CLI has no new commands or flags in this release.
**v0.22.1 was tagged but never published.** v0.22.2 supersedes it, so roll v0.22.2 and pin modules to v0.22.2.

**A move becomes ready when little is left to copy.** By default, a preparing round now promotes when it copied 16 MiB or less. To change that bar, set `CARLOS_MOVE_READY_DELTA_BYTES` in `/etc/carlos/host.env`; the agent reads it when it starts. `0` restores the old rule that a round must copy nothing. A value that is not a whole number of bytes is ignored with a log line, and the default stays. The ready log line now shows the bytes copied, the number of changes and the bar.

**Copy receipts in the source box's data bucket.** A box moving an instance away keeps receipts at `move-receipts/<host>.json` in its own data bucket, so large objects that have not changed are not copied again. The cut and an abort delete them. A deployment whose data-bucket policy denies DeleteObject keeps stale receipts, which are harmless. The box policy in this repo already allows the prefix.

**The cut is still exact.** It copies everything that is left before it flips the record. If an object changes during that final copy, the cut waits for the next pass instead of landing an incomplete copy.

**The Database tile is console only.** It reads the database sizes boxes have reported since v0.21.0, so it needs no box roll and no env or IAM change. A slow read shows a dash and never holds up the page.

bullets.md: **Availability, apart from errors.** `carlos availability` lists the requests an app's instances could not answer, every 502, 503 and 504 the edge saw, grouped by cause instead of by page. One outage is one row, however many pages it hit. `--fp <id>` expands a cause to each request and the path it asked for. The same view is the new Availability tab beside Errors.
**Errors is shorter.** `carlos errors` and the Errors tab keep the app's own 500s and the error lines in its logs. Edge 502s, 503s and 504s, failed wakes and exits have moved to Availability.

**Replica instances.** `carlos instances create --role replica --region <r>` makes a second instance of an app, holding a one-way copy of the live instance's data, in a region near its buyers. The live instance names the regions it allows replicas in with `--replicas ie,uk` when it is created. Until a batch of orders drains home, a replica holds order data in its own region, so the regions are always a decision on the live instance, never a default.

**Door keys.** `carlos instances door-key create`, `list` and `revoke` manage keys for the edge-local door. That is one socket on a box that a process running beside an app's instances can dial to reach any of them, whether it is asleep, moved to another box or awake. A key is shown once, when it is created. The door is off until the box's operator turns it on.
**Faster log reads.** Log chunks are now fetched 16 at a time instead of one by one, which speeds up `carlos logs`, Errors and Availability.
**A restored app keeps its pipeline.** When the console registers an app whose files are already in the bucket, it keeps that app's release pipeline instead of resetting it to the default.

**Roll the console first, then the boxes, close together.** The boxes record why the edge had no answer and the console shows it. A console on its own groups stored 502s under "cause not recorded", and new ones too until the boxes roll. Boxes on their own, under an old console, list each cause as its own row on Errors. Rolling the console back is safe: nothing in the bucket is rewritten.

**A new CLI against an old console.** `carlos availability` fails with `not found: check --account and --app, and that your token's address is a member`. Until the console rolls, that message means the console predates the command, not that the app or your membership is missing. An old console silently ignores `carlos instances create --role replica` and creates an ordinary instance in that region instead.

**No replicas until every box has rolled.** Only this release keeps replicas out of DNS latency routing. Each box adds two columns to its registry when it starts (`routes.replicas` and `routes.replica`). There is nothing to migrate, and a box rolled back ignores them.

**Long polls show up in Availability.** A visitor who gives up after waiting five seconds or more, before the instance has sent response headers, is filed as an outage. On a sleeping route the five seconds include the wake. An endpoint that holds its headers longer by design, like a long poll, shows a standing row, and that row is expected. A visitor who leaves sooner is no longer filed at all, so expect fewer one-off 502s on static files.
**Tunnelled failures are filed once.** On a route a box reaches over a tunnel or a fleet, the front box files only its own hop failures, and the box serving the app files the rest.

**Instance moves.** A box cutting a move now fences the instance so a scheduled wake cannot start it again mid-move. A move past ready can no longer be aborted, and a replica cannot be moved: delete it and create one in the new region. A later release's boxes rely on this console's abort rule, which is one more reason to roll the console first.

**The edge-local door is off by default.** It stays off until a box sets `CARLOS_EDGE_DOOR=/run/carlos/edge-local.sock` and its agent restarts. The calling process's user must also be enrolled with `carlos bootstrap --socket-consumer <user>`. The console re-signs door keys every 12 hours, and a key whose record has not been re-signed for 72 hours stops working, so a console down that long closes every door.

**Each instance gets its own `/dev/shm`.** Instance units no longer see the host's `/dev/shm`, so an instance cannot reach another's shared memory. They also no longer set `RestrictSUIDSGID=`, which broke `openat2` on systemd 257 and kept the isolated exec probe from reporting ready. `carlos system update` installs the new units, and a running instance picks them up when it next restarts.

notes.md:
#### Region residence: instances know where they live, and can move

This release is about placement. Three pieces land together (platform #329, #331, #346):

- **Armed-placement validation on instance create** (#329). Creating an instance names a region, and the console now refuses a code that is not armed on the deployment instead of provisioning into nowhere. Each box's `edges` file publishes its own placement code, and every exec child inherits it as `CARLOS_REGION`, so an app can tell where it is running without asking anyone.
- **Two-phase, data-following instance moves** (#331). `POST .../instances/{host}/move` requests a move to another armed region; the host prepares in rounds, mirroring the instance's replica prefix into the destination's staging bucket until the copy is current; `POST .../move/cut` then cuts over, with a re-checkpoint at the cut so nothing written in the gap is lost. `DELETE .../move` aborts cleanly at either phase. Staging wins over a stale local copy, a failed fallback is a hard fail rather than a silent downgrade, and a serial nudge on every box-side write means the cut chain converges in seconds rather than five-minute hops.
- **The armed-regions endpoint** (#346). `GET /api/cli/apps/{account}/{app}/regions` returns the deployment's regions with their `armed` state, the home region's name, and the default, so pickers in the console, the CLI, and consumer apps draw from one list.

#### Also in this release

- **`served_by` on instances** (#337): an instance row now carries where it is *observed* to be served (the edges that actually join it), beside where it was *placed*.
- **Control and edges files carry placement + data-bucket coordinates**, so a box and its peers can locate each other's replica prefixes without a console round trip.
- **`sibling_staging_arns`** on the `region-remote-host` and region-host Terraform modules: the push-only `moves/*` grant that lets a host stage into a sibling region's bucket and nothing else.
- **`carlos-app@` units can no longer reach IMDS** (#351/#352); a `host_role` drop-in re-opens it for the apps that need instance credentials.

The operator CLI verbs are unchanged from v0.16.0; the new surface is on the console API and in the host, edge, and activator halves of the same binary.

#### carlos features — app feature flags on the deployment object

The headline: `carlos features set` and `carlos features list` (platform #347, PR #350). An app's own feature flags — switches the app defines, the platform stores, serves and audits, but never interprets:

```sh
carlos features set --app titogo sandbox=on
carlos features list --app titogo
```

`key=` with nothing after the equals clears a key. The app reads the map off the `deployment` block its instance token already fetches (beside `managed_domains`), so a change lands on the app's next poll — no restart, no env edit, no root-owned file on an edge box. Setting is an admin-role write; the app's own credential can read its flags but never set them.

#### Also in this release

- **Custom domains grew a lifecycle** (#299, #325, #328): `carlos domains list` rows now carry one derived `state` (`checking`, `pending-dns`, `misdirected`, `issuing-cert`, `live`, `unknown`) with a `reason`, structured `records[]` telling you exactly which DNS records to create, and a `checked_at` freshness stamp; the answer's self-describing `deployment` block says what the deployment manages. A per-host read (`GET .../domains/{host}` under the hood) makes single-hostname refreshes cheap.
- **`carlos deploy` is stricter about what it claims**: it refuses a git-derived version from a dirty tree, and watches the app's own build report rather than an edge header.
- **`carlos apps create`** gained `-control-plane` and `-build-probe`.

notes.md:
#### CLI flag conventions

The documented face of every carlos command now says `--app`. Both spellings have always parsed identically — Go's flag package treats `-app` and `--app` the same — so this release changes what the tool teaches, not what it accepts: usage pages, docs, and error messages all show the double-dash form, and the four flags you type all day gain short aliases:

```
--app, -a        --channel, -c
--environment, -e  --version, -v
```

The old single-dash spellings (`-app`, `-channel`, …) keep working forever; nothing you have scripted breaks. Every command's `-h` page is now generated from the live flag set through one usage printer, so a usage page can no longer drift from what the parser actually accepts. (#321)

#### Licence

The platform source is now MPL-2.0, following the redaction pass ahead of the repository going public. (#317)

#### For operators

The same binary is the edge, the host agent, and the console, so this tag also carries fleet-side work:

- **Non-issuer certificate backfill** (#320, #318): certsync backfills certificates into `control/certs/` on every contending box, not just the issuance winner, with identity settle stamps — a box that never wins issuance still converges the certificates it serves.
- **Delegated customer wildcards on every edge** (#311, #305): the edges file publishes delegated wildcards and every edge loads them, closing the last name-scope gap for serving custom names through region edges.
- **Fleet architecture page** (#237): the console renders `/fleet/architecture`, an architecture diagram drawn from a provider-neutral inventory of the fleet.

---

Nothing in this tag changes what existing scripts parse — `-app` and friends behave exactly as before.

notes.md:
#### carlos economics backhaul

What serving through region edges costs the platform. When a request lands on a region edge and is carried on to the account's home box, the inter-region leg is a cost the platform absorbs — it sits inside the account's egress total, never on top of it, and appears in nobody's bill. This verb is the operator's view of that leg:

```
carlos economics backhaul [-period mtd|last|7d]
```

Per account: bytes backhauled, the share of that account's egress it represents, and what the leg comes to at the rate card's inter-region $/GB. The header shows the period's coverage (days of meters present) so a partial month reads as one. Backhaul meters are a subset of the egress meters and are never counted as usage. Operator only — a non-operator's token gets the same bare 404 an unknown route gets. (#288, #284)

`carlos economics` with no sub-verb now lists both `bill` and `backhaul`.

#### Multi-region ingress, hardened

The same binary is the edge and the host agent, so this tag also carries the steering work that has been rolling out across the fleet:

- **Custom domains through any edge** (#287): the edges file publishes attached custom domains under their own names, aliases are marked on the wire, routes win collisions, and the config layer denies entry for names that must not be published.
- **Wildcard parents** (#300, #290): derived from the deployment's hosts — provisioned routes as well as console-minted ones — with the class mark on the wire, a serialized refresh, and an async wake that is blind to catch-alls.
- **Per-box domain health stamps** (#303, #304): run on every box again, once per tick, never on a fleet box, inert without an apps domain; a resolver failure never overwrites a DNS verdict.
- **Certificate backfill** (#291, #297): the issuer backfills pre-existing certificates into `control/certs/`, with the settled stamp pinned on the bucket side.
- **Domains reconcile is a housekeeper duty** (#289): one writer per deployment.

notes.md:
#### A static site gets a URL from the CLI alone

`carlos deploy -kind static` with no `-host` now mints the app's own platform hostname — `<app>.<sqid>.<apps-domain>` — and the static route record that serves it. Publishing a site no longer requires owning a domain or pointing DNS at anything:

```
carlos apps create -app mysite
carlos deploy -kind static ./dist
```

Everything it needs was already there: DNS under the apps domain resolves to the edge at any depth, and the edge derives its own per-account wildcard certificate from the live route table. The missing piece was a record, and now the CLI writes one.

`-host` still does exactly what it did — it now means "serve on this hostname instead of the app's own", and remains the answer for a domain you control.

#### carlos instances set-channel

The only door onto which release channel a route follows. A route's channel lives in its instance record, which the box converges from every pass, so `carlos route -channel` on a box is reverted within seconds — and until now nothing else could change it. A route that landed on the wrong channel had a URL that served nothing and no way back.

```
carlos instances set-channel -app <a> -host <h> -channel <c>
```

A move must clear the rules of **both** channels it touches, each at its strictest, because a move can achieve a promotion: with `production` requiring approvals and `edge` requiring none, moving the production route onto edge would otherwise serve unreviewed code from a guarded URL with nobody's approval. Gated moves are proposed and confirmed in the console, exactly like a promote.

#### carlos instances create -kind

`instance` (default) | `service` | `static` — exposing the route class the record shape has always carried.

#### carlos schedule

Recurring and one-shot work per app, owned by the platform rather than by a
box's crontab: `carlos schedule ls | set | rm | run`. Landed in #285 and
included in this tag; boxes and consoles are already rolled for it.

notes.md:
#### Tenant email — `carlos email`

An app on CARLOS can now send mail without running an MTA or holding a cloud key. The platform mints a sending identity, publishes DKIM, SPF and DMARC where it owns the zone, and delivers working SMTP credentials as config.

```
carlos email enable -app <app>
```

That is the whole walk: declare, provision the domain, wait for verification, deliver. The identity defaults to the app's own host, so the signing domain matches the domain of the links inside the mail. Credentials arrive as `CARLOS_SMTP_HOST`, `_PORT`, `_USER`, `_PASS`, `_FROM` (rename the set with `-env-prefix`). Transport is submission on 587 with STARTTLS.

For a customer's own domain, `-domain mail.example.com` prints the record set for the zone's owner to publish and polls until SES confirms it.

The rest of the surface:

| Verb | What it does |
|---|---|
| `carlos email status` | What is declared, which domains verified, what was delivered |
| `carlos email test -to <addr>` | Sends a real message through a throwaway credential, then revokes it |
| `carlos email domains add` | Add a second sending domain |
| `carlos email credentials create\|list\|revoke` | Standalone credentials for something not on CARLOS; the password is shown once |
| `carlos email rotate [-finish]` | Two-phase key rotation |
| `carlos email pause\|resume` | A deployment operator's abuse brake |

##### Three things worth knowing

- **A freshly minted credential does not work for the first minute or two.** SES's SMTP endpoint does not see a new IAM access key immediately, and the symptom is `535 Authentication Credentials Invalid` — which reads exactly like a wrong password and is not one. `carlos email test` now waits this out; an app's own first sends after `enable` will still meet it.
- **DMARC passes on the DKIM rail alone.** Records are published with `adkim=s; aspf=s`, and that strictness is what stops one tenant's signature authenticating another tenant's From address on a shared domain. SPF authenticates but does not *align*, because the envelope sender is a region-qualified subdomain. So never turn off DKIM signing on a sending identity, and treat `p=reject` as safe but unforgiving.
- **The MAIL FROM subdomain carries its region forever**, fixed at first verification. On a custom domain it lives in the customer's zone — the one record CARLOS cannot republish for them.

#### Also in this release

- **Multi-region steering** is member-settable and pool-railed.
- `carlos email status` names a verified domain that emits no SES events, rather than showing counts that can only ever be zero.

notes.md:
#### Windows

`carlos` now runs on Windows as a **client**: `carlos login`, `ship`, `deploy`,
`logs` — everything that talks to a console or a bucket — from a Windows
workstation against a Linux fleet. Download `carlos-windows-amd64.zip` (or
`-arm64`), unpack `carlos.exe` onto your `PATH`, and check it against
`SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Two things to know:

- **`carlos update` does not self-replace on Windows.** Windows cannot rename a
  new binary over a running `.exe`, so `carlos update` tells you when you're
  behind and hands you the zip URL instead of swapping itself.
- **Your credentials file is not permission-protected on Windows.** On Linux and
  macOS `~/.carlos/credentials` is written `0600`; the equivalent mode means
  nothing on `%USERPROFILE%\.carlos\credentials`. Don't `carlos login` on a
  shared machine.

Windows cannot BE a box — `carlos agent` and the root-side passes need unix
sockets, `flock` and systemd, and refuse there rather than pretending.

#### Also in this release

105 commits since v0.9.0, including:

- **Service principals** (#227) — non-human members that deploy.
- **Edge response compression** (#224, #230) — gzip on the shared edge.
- **Logs terminal pane** (#209) in the console.
- **SQLite corruption defence** (#200) and replica/hibernate freshness work
  (#211, #214, #213).
- **Wake single-flight** (#199), fleet claims (#215), economics account names (#203).

#### Verifying

Every artifact's checksum is in `SHA256SUMS.txt`, signed with the CLI-update key
as `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` — the same signature `carlos update` checks against the
public key embedded in the binary.
